posts.md:
## Accessibility at IIT Madras

IIT Madras is committed to creating an inclusive campus where students with disabilities can learn, participate, and thrive independently.

The institute supports accessibility through infrastructure, academic accommodations, assistive technologies, student support systems, and continuous improvements across the campus.

## Physical Accessibility

To improve accessibility across its campus, IIT Madras provides:

- Ramps and support railings in most academic buildings, hostels, and common halls/auditoriums.
- Elevators in multi-storey buildings (accessible with assistance when required).
- Accessible washrooms in several academic and hostel blocks.
- Battery-operated vehicles on a need basis to support easier movement across the campus.

The institute continues to improve accessibility, with newer construction projects incorporating inclusive design from the planning stage.

## Academic Support

Students with disabilities can receive academic accommodations based on their individual requirements.

These include:

- Additional examination time.
- Scribes or laptops during examinations.
- Assistive technologies such as screen readers and text-to-speech tools through the Central Library and the Dean of Students (DoST) Office.
- Flexibility in deadlines, attendance, or evaluation methods where appropriate, in consultation with faculty.

## Support for Visual Disabilities

Students with visual disabilities have access to:

- Screen-reading software such as **NVDA** and **JAWS**.
- Digital study materials in accessible formats (such as accessible PDFs and ePub files).
- Tactile diagrams and Braille-enabled content through collaborations with research labs and the **Accessibility Research Centre (ARC)**.

## Support for Hearing Impairments

Support available includes:

- Written transcripts or subtitles for recorded lectures and presentations.
- Real-time captioning or note-taking services on request.
- Seating arrangements that facilitate lip-reading or proximity to interpreters during in-person sessions.

## Student Support Network

Students can seek assistance from several support systems across the institute:

- **Faculty Advisors (FacAds)** help coordinate academic accommodations and communicate with instructors.
- The **Dean of Students (DoST) Office** supports documentation and learning accommodations.
- **MITR** and **SAATHI** provide peer support, mentorship, and emotional well-being initiatives.
- The **Campus Hospital** provides general healthcare services.

Students often receive additional support from peers across hostels, classrooms, clubs, and samitis, contributing to an inclusive campus environment.

## Accessibility Research Centre (ARC)

The **Accessibility Research Centre (ARC)**, housed within the **Department of Computer Science and Engineering**, develops technologies and solutions that promote accessibility and inclusive design.

Its work includes:

- Tactile interfaces
- Accessible software
- Assistive technologies

The centre's innovations support individuals both within and beyond the IIT Madras community.

## Scholarships & Institute Support

Students admitted under the **PwD category** are eligible for:

- Government scholarships offered through the **Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD)** via the **National Scholarship Portal (NSP)**.
- Fee concessions.
- Institutional assistance provided by IIT Madras.

## Growing Towards Greater Accessibility

IIT Madras continues to improve accessibility across its campus.

While some older buildings and forested pathways still require upgrades, the institute remains committed to integrating inclusive design into future infrastructure and campus services, ensuring a more accessible and supportive environment for all students.

topics.summary: The 75% attendance rule and everything a P grade affects.

posts.md:
## When do you get a P?

Students are expected to maintain **100% attendance**, especially because IITM is a residential institute and academics is the core activity.

However, a minimum of **75% attendance** is required to avoid a **P (Poor Attendance)** grade.

The 25% flexibility is intended to accommodate situations such as:

- Short-term medical requirements
- Family functions
- Off-campus interviews
- Exams
- Other genuine requirements

>  The 75% attendance should not be treated as the target. Students are expected to attend classes regularly.

## Keep Track of Your Attendance

IITM uses an app-based attendance management system that allows students to keep track of their attendance.

Make sure you monitor your attendance regularly.

## Consequences of a P Grade

### POR

Students with a **P grade are excluded from applying for PORs**.

### Supplementary Examination

If you have a **P attendance code in a course**, you **cannot apply for the supplementary examination for that course**.

### Minor

If you have a **P grade in any course belonging to your Minor stream**, you **cannot claim the Minor**.

>  **Exception:** Students in their **final semester** can still claim the Minor even if they have a P in a course belonging to the Minor stream.

### Attendance as Class Participation

Faculty may choose to **incentivize attendance through marks/class participation**.

### Parent Alert

Parents may be **alerted if a student's attendance is poor**.

## Additional Rules for P Grades

### SEAT Elective Allotment

Students with **no P grades** will be considered first for elective allotment in SEAT.

Then students will be considered based on the number of P grades:

**0 P → 1 P → 2 P → 3 P → ...**

The SEAT rule uses a **rolling 1-year window**.

This means students are encouraged to improve their attendance over time.

### IDDD Allotment

Students with **no P grades** will be considered first during IDDD allotment.

Those with **1 P** will be considered after them, followed by those with 2 P, 3 P, and so on.

For IDDD allotment, **all attendance data collected up to that point** will be considered.

### 3 or More P Grades

Students with **more than 3 P grades during their tenure at IITM** will not be eligible for consideration for:

IDDD upgradation
Dual Degree upgradation
MSc/MTech → PhD upgradation
YRF
Honours

### Remember

A P grade can affect your **exams, POR eligibility, Minor, elective allotment, and eligibility for certain academic opportunities**.

So, keep track of your attendance and attend classes regularly.

## About IIT Madras Thaiyur (Discovery) Campus

The **Thaiyur Campus**, officially known as the **Discovery Campus**, is the second campus of IIT Madras. Located approximately **36 km from the main Guindy campus**, it spans around **163 acres** and has been developed as a dedicated hub for **research, innovation, and technology development**.

Unlike the main campus, which focuses on academics, student life, and residential facilities, the Thaiyur campus is designed to support **advanced research**, **industry collaborations**, and **large-scale interdisciplinary projects**.

## Why was it built?

As IIT Madras expanded its research activities, the main campus faced space constraints for setting up large laboratories and research centres. The Discovery Campus was established to:

- Support cutting-edge research across multiple disciplines.
- Provide world-class laboratory and testing facilities.
- Encourage collaboration between academia, industry, and government.
- Enable long-term research projects that require specialized infrastructure.

## Key Highlights

- Located in **Thaiyur**, about **36 km from the Guindy campus**.
- Spread across **163 acres**.
- Dedicated primarily to **research and innovation**.
- Promotes collaboration with industries, startups, and government organizations.
- Focuses on solving real-world engineering and scientific challenges.

## Major Research Areas

Research at the Discovery Campus spans several emerging fields, including:

- Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning
- Robotics & Autonomous Systems
- Sustainable Energy & Green Hydrogen
- Climate Science & Environmental Engineering
- Smart Infrastructure & Urban Technologies
- Materials Science & Advanced Manufacturing
- Ports, Waterways & Coastal Engineering
- Data Science & High-Performance Computing

## Facilities

The campus is planned with state-of-the-art infrastructure, including:

- Advanced research laboratories
- Common instrumentation facilities
- Innovation and incubation spaces
- Industry collaboration centres
- Conference and seminar halls
- Research scholar hostels
- Specialized testing and experimentation facilities

## Who uses the Thaiyur Campus?

The campus is primarily intended for:

- PhD Scholars
- MTech/MS Research Students
- Faculty Researchers
- Research Staff
- Industry Collaborators
- Startup and Innovation Teams

Undergraduate students may visit the campus for research projects, internships, workshops, or specialized laboratory work.

## Why is it important?

The Discovery Campus represents IIT Madras' vision of becoming a global leader in research and innovation. It provides the infrastructure needed to develop next-generation technologies, support interdisciplinary research, and strengthen partnerships with industries and government organizations.

## In Simple Words

> **Think of the Guindy campus as the place where students learn, and the Thaiyur (Discovery) campus as the place where new technologies are created.** While the main campus focuses on education and student life, the Thaiyur campus focuses on research, innovation, and solving real-world problems.

## What is CFI?

**Centre For Innovation (CFI)** is the **largest student-run innovation lab in India**. It is housed in the **Sudha and Shankar Innovation Hub** and serves as a launchpad for students to transform their ideas into real products.

> **"Walk in with an idea, walk out with a product!"**

The CFI building is **alumni-funded**, reflecting the strong senior-junior and alumni network built through CFI clubs and competition teams.

## Can Students Join?

Yes! CFI is open to all students.

CFI consists of:

- **13 Clubs**
- **6 Competition Teams**

Applications for clubs are released during the **first semester**.

The application process includes:

- Filling out an application form (no prerequisites).
- Assessment of skills and eagerness to learn.
- An interview conducted by the respective club heads.

CFI has **no fixed timings** and is **open 24×7**, allowing students to work on projects whenever they wish.

## Life at CFI

CFI is a builders' paradise, bustling with activity throughout the day.

Students have dedicated workspaces for every club and competition team, where they work on innovative projects using the institute's infrastructure and funding support.

Projects undertaken at CFI often leave a lasting impact on students and continue to influence their careers even after graduation.

The Centre stands as a testament to engineering in its truest sense—building, innovating, and solving real-world problems.

## CFI Clubs

The clubs work throughout the year on multiple projects, with separate teams assigned to each project.

Some projects aim for **patents**, while many are showcased at **Open House**, an annual exhibition attended by professors, industry professionals, and media.

### Clubs at CFI

- 3-D Printing Club
- Aero Club
- AI Club
- Biotech Club
- Electronics Club
- Horizon
- i-Bot Club
- Mathematics Club
- Product Design Club
- Programming Club
- Team Envisage
- Team Sahaay
- WebOps and Blockchain Club

## Competition Teams

The competition teams represent **IIT Madras** at prestigious national and international competitions.

### Raftaar Formula Racing

Builds Formula-style race cars and represents IIT Madras in international Formula Student competitions.

### Team Abhiyaan

Develops intelligent, robust, precise, and safe autonomous ground navigation systems.

### Team Anveshak

Designs and builds remote-operated all-terrain rovers with robotic manipulators and diggers for harsh Martian conditions.

### Avishkar Hyperloop

Works on sustainable Hyperloop technologies aimed at revolutionizing transportation.

### Team Agnirath

Builds state-of-the-art solar-powered cars for a sustainable future.

### Team Abhyuday

Focused on rocketry and advancing space technology through student-led innovation.

## CFI Summer School

Apart from clubs and competition teams, CFI conducts a **Summer School**.

It helps students from both within and outside IIT Madras learn the basics of each club through concise introductory sessions, providing an overview of the work carried out at CFI.

## CFI Legacy

CFI is one of the strongest enablers of the builder culture at IIT Madras.

It provides students with the infrastructure, funding, and environment needed to transform ideas into impactful innovations.

One of CFI's most notable success stories is **Ather Energy**.

Founded by **Tarun Mehta** and **Swapnil Jain**, alumni of the Engineering Design Department at IIT Madras, Ather began as an electric vehicle prototype developed at CFI before growing into one of India's leading electric vehicle companies.

> **If you're passionate about building, innovating, and creating technology from scratch, CFI is the place to be.**

topics.title: CGPA: does it matter?
topics.summary: Minimum 5.0, and how CGPA affects DD/IDDD, exchange, internships, placements, higher studies.

posts.md:
Yes. While the importance of a **CGPA** depends on your goals, it remains an important measure of your academic performance.

CGPA acts as a primary and objective filter for:

- Recruiters
- Scholarship Boards
- Universities

It reflects your:

- Academic consistency
- Discipline
- Ability to meet academic expectations

Although CGPA is not the only factor considered, it plays a significant role in many academic and career opportunities.

## Academic Continuation

Students are required to maintain a **minimum CGPA of 5.0** at the end of every semester.

If a student's CGPA falls below **5.0**:

- An academic warning is issued.
- Parents are informed.

A **successive reduction** in CGPA (remaining below **5.0** across two semesters) can result in **termination from the programme**.

For the **Online BS Programme**:

- A minimum overall **CGPA of 6.0** is required across Foundation and Diploma courses.
- A minimum **CGPA of 8.0** is required to progress to the **PG Diploma / BS Degree Level**.

## Academic Opportunities

A higher CGPA provides greater academic flexibility and access to several opportunities.

These include:

- Higher semester credit limits.
- Eligibility for a **Dual Degree** (minimum CGPA of **8.0**).
- Eligibility for certain department-specific programmes and competitive **IDDD specialisations** (such as **Quantitative Finance** or **Data Science**), where a **CGPA above 8.5** may be required.
- Better chances of being nominated for **Semester Exchange Programmes**, where CGPA is used as a selection criterion.

A lower CGPA may limit access to these opportunities.

## Internships & Placements

Many companies use CGPA as an initial screening criterion during internship and placement processes.

This is especially common in sectors such as:

- Software
- Consulting
- Finance

Companies such as **Google** and **Goldman Sachs** may use CGPA for resume shortlisting.

Academic and research internships, both in India and abroad, also place significant importance on CGPA.

Examples include:

- Mitacs Globalink (Canada)
- Charpak Summer Training Scholarship (France)

A **CGPA above 8.5** is generally considered sufficient to keep most opportunities open.

## Higher Studies

For postgraduate studies such as **Master's** and **PhD** programmes, CGPA is one of the most important indicators of academic performance.

A strong CGPA (typically **8.5 or above**) is often expected for admission to highly competitive institutions and scholarship programmes.

Examples include:

- McGill McBain Scholarship
- MEXT Scholarship

## Key Takeaway

CGPA is not the only factor considered for internships, placements, scholarships, or higher studies, but it remains an important screening criterion.

Maintaining a good CGPA helps keep more academic and career opportunities open while giving you greater flexibility throughout your degree.

topics.title: CGPA: how it's calculated
topics.summary: The formula, grade points (S=10 … E=5, U), relative vs absolute grading.

posts.md:
IIT Madras follows a **10-point grading system** to calculate a student's **Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA)**.

CGPA is calculated as the **weighted average of the grade points earned across all successfully completed courses**, taking into account the credits assigned to each course.

### Formula

**CGPA = Σ(Cᵢ × GPᵢ) / ΣCᵢ**

Where:

- **Cᵢ** = Credits assigned to the course
- **GPᵢ** = Grade Point earned in the course
- **Σ** = Sum over all successfully completed courses across all semesters

## Grade Points

The corresponding grade points are:

| Grade | Grade Point |
|------|------------:|
| S | 10 |
| A | 9 |
| B | 8 |
| C | 7 |
| D | 6 |
| E | 5 |
| U / W | 0 |

- **U Grade** indicates that the student has **not passed the course**.
- IIT Madras **does not award ranks or divisions** based on CGPA.

## Relative vs Absolute Grading

Grades at IIT Madras are awarded using either **Relative Grading** or **Absolute Grading**, depending on the course instructor.

## Relative Grading

In relative grading:

- Grades are based on your performance **relative to the rest of the class**.
- Typically, the **top 5–10%** of the class receive an **S Grade**.
- Other grades are determined using the class average and standard deviation.

## Absolute Grading

In absolute grading:

- Grades are awarded based on **predefined score thresholds**.
- For example, an **S Grade** may require a score of **90% or above**.

The grading method for a course is decided by the **course instructor**.

## Academic Requirements

Students must maintain a **minimum CGPA of 5.0**.

Falling below this threshold or repeatedly failing courses may lead to:

- Academic Probation
- Termination from the programme

Students who wish to pursue a **Dual Degree** must have a **minimum CGPA of 8.0**.

## Why Does CGPA Matter?

The importance of CGPA depends on your academic and career goals.

It is commonly used as an initial screening criterion for:

- Placements and internships at companies such as Microsoft and Google.
- Admissions to higher education and research institutions, including universities such as Stanford and institutes like the Max Planck Institutes in Germany.

A strong CGPA helps keep more academic and career opportunities open.

posts.md:
**How Course Registration Works at IITM**

Every semester, you need to register for the courses you want to take. The entire process happens through the **Workflow** portal:

workflow.iitm.ac.in/student

There are **4 main steps**:

**1. Registration (before the semester)**

- Register online through Workflow using your **LDAP login**
- You can change your course choices until the **registration deadline**
- Your **Faculty Advisor (FA)** then reviews and approves your registration

** Credit Limit**

From the **5th semester onwards**, your maximum credit limit depends on your **CGPA**:

- **CGPA 8.5+** → Maximum **75 credits**
- **CGPA 8.0–8.5** → Maximum **70 credits**
- **CGPA below 8.0** → Maximum **66 credits**

Your **Faculty Advisor can lower your credit limit, but cannot increase it**.

The credit limit applies for the **whole semester**.

So, when choosing your courses, make sure your total credits stay within the limit applicable to you.

**2. SEAT (Electives)**

**SEAT = Student Elective Allocation Tool**

SEAT is the system that **allots elective seats based on the preferences you enter during registration**.

During registration, you enter your preferences for the electives you want to take.

**Priority:**
Students with **0 P grades** get priority first, followed by students with **1 P grade**, then **2 P grades**, and so on.

- If you don't enter any elective preferences, you **won't be allotted any elective**
- SEAT results are sent to you by **email from Workflow**

**3. Enrolment (start of semester)**

For **BTech students**:

- If you've **paid your fees**, you are enrolled automatically once your attendance is marked on **Digii**
- There is **nothing you need to do manually** for enrolment

**4. Add/Drop (first few weeks)**

If you want to change your courses after the semester starts, Add/Drop is done through the **same Workflow portal**.

- **BTech/BS/DD students** get the first couple of days before everyone else
- The **Add window closes first**
- The **Drop window opens a bit later**
- The **drop deadline is never extended**
- Your **credit limit still applies** when adding courses
- Workflow can become very slow during Add/Drop week, so **don't wait until the last day**
**Questions?**

**Course-related queries:**
helpdeskcourses@iitm.ac.in **only**

**Technical registration issues:**
Raise a Workflow ticket under **"Course Registration"**

or contact:
helpdeskworkflow@iitm.ac.in

topics.title: Credits
topics.summary: What credits are, 400–405 to graduate, credit limits by CGPA, unallotted and HSS credits.

posts.md:
A **credit** is a measure of the academic workload associated with a course.

Every course you take—whether it is:

- Core Courses
- Laboratory Courses
- Electives
- Humanities Courses
- Management Courses
- Projects

carries a certain number of credits.

As you complete courses, these credits accumulate towards your graduation requirements.

Graduation is determined **not by the number of years spent in the programme**, but by successfully completing the required number of credits prescribed in the curriculum.

## Credit Requirements

For most **B.Tech programmes (2025 batch onwards)**, the graduation requirement is **400–405 credits**, depending on the department.

Examples:

- Computational Engineering & Mechanics — **400 Credits**
- Aerospace Engineering — **405 Credits**

A typical semester carries around **45–60 credits**, with the workload generally being higher during the initial years due to core courses and laboratory sessions.

### Maximum Credit Limit (From Semester 5)

The maximum number of credits a student can register depends on their **CGPA**:

| CGPA | Maximum Credits |
|------|----------------:|
| **8.5 and above** | 75 |
| **8.0 – 8.5** | 70 |
| **Below 8.0** | 66 |

This flexibility allows students to pursue opportunities such as electives, minors, honours, and dual degrees.

## What are Unallotted Credits?

Many curricula include a significant number of **Unallotted Credits**.

These credits are intentionally kept flexible and can be used for:

- Department Electives
- Free Electives
- Minor Programmes
- Interdisciplinary Studies
- Additional Specialisation Courses
- Exchange Programmes or Internships (subject to institute rules)

These credits allow students to personalise their degree based on their interests and career goals.

## Humanities & Management Courses

In addition to technical courses, every **B.Tech student** must complete **27 compulsory credits** of **Humanities and Management** courses.

These courses expose students to areas such as:

- Economics
- Psychology
- Languages (German, French, Korean)
- Communication
- Management
- Public Policy

They help students develop broader perspectives, critical thinking, and communication skills alongside their technical education.

## Credits in a Dual Degree

A **Dual Degree** combines a **B.Tech** with an additional postgraduate degree.

Since students complete the requirements for two degrees, the total credit requirement is higher.

Depending on the programme, students are required to complete approximately **500–550 credits**.

For example:

- **B.Tech + M.Tech in Biological Engineering** — **521 Credits**
- **Corresponding B.Tech Programme** — **400 Credits**

The additional credits primarily come from:

- Advanced Postgraduate Courses
- Research Work
- Thesis or Project Requirements
- Higher-level Electives

## Why are Credits Important?

Credits ensure that every student completes the required coursework, laboratory training, projects, and electives necessary for their programme.

They determine:

- Progress towards graduation
- Eligibility for programmes such as Minors and Honours
- The flexibility to explore areas beyond your core discipline

In simple terms, **credits are the academic currency of your degree**. Every course contributes credits, and you become eligible to graduate once you have accumulated the required total while satisfying all curriculum requirements.

posts.md:
The **Interdisciplinary Dual Degree (IDDD)** program at IIT Madras allows students to convert their **4-year B.Tech.** into a **5-year Dual Degree**, enabling them to graduate with:

- **B.Tech.** in their original department.
- **M.Tech.** in an interdisciplinary specialization.

The program is designed to promote interdisciplinary learning, allowing students to combine knowledge from different fields and build expertise that is highly valued in both industry and academia.

## Eligibility

Students can apply for IDDD:

- **At the end of the 5th semester.**
- **Minimum CGPA:** 8.0 (subject to institute regulations and programme availability).

Upon selection, the student's degree duration extends from **4 years to 5 years**.

## How is IDDD Different from a Dual Degree (DD)?

## Dual Degree (DD)

In a regular Dual Degree programme, students pursue both their Bachelor's and Master's degrees within the **same or closely related discipline**.

**Example:**
- B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering + M.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering.

The primary focus is on gaining deeper specialization in a single field.

### Interdisciplinary Dual Degree (IDDD)

In an IDDD, students pursue their Bachelor's degree in one discipline and their Master's degree in a **different interdisciplinary field**.

**Example:**
- B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering + M.Tech. in Data Science.

This allows students to explore new domains while building on the knowledge gained in their core branch.

## Available IDDD Programmes

Students can currently opt for IDDD in the following areas:

- Advanced Materials and Nanotechnology
- Complex Systems and Dynamics
- Biomedical Engineering
- Computational Engineering
- Cyber-Physical Systems
- Data Science
- Electric Vehicles
- Energy Systems
- Robotics
- Quantum Science and Technology
- Quantitative Finance
- Public Policy
- Tech MBA

> *The list of available programmes may change based on institute offerings.*

## Benefits of IDDD

## Interdisciplinary Learning

Study two different disciplines and develop a broader understanding beyond your core engineering branch.

## Better Problem Solving

Learning across multiple domains helps students approach problems from different perspectives, encouraging creativity and innovation.

## Better Career Opportunities

Graduates possess a unique combination of skills that can open doors to careers in technology, finance, consulting, research, healthcare, energy, and many other interdisciplinary fields.

## Research Opportunities

The programme encourages interdisciplinary research, allowing students to work on problems that combine concepts from multiple fields.

## Should You Choose IDDD?

IDDD is a great option if you:

- Have a strong academic record.
- Want to explore a field beyond your core branch.
- Are interested in interdisciplinary research.
- Wish to gain expertise in emerging domains.
- Are comfortable spending one additional year to earn an integrated B.Tech. + M.Tech. degree.

> **IDDD is an excellent opportunity for students who want to combine their engineering background with emerging fields such as Data Science, Robotics, Quantum Technology, Public Policy, or Tech MBA, making them well-prepared for future careers and research.**

posts.md:
**Education Loans at IIT Madras**

An education loan is money you borrow to pay for your studies and repay later with interest.

**Where can you get one?**

- **Banks:** Government and private banks offer education loans. SBI and Canara Bank have branches on the IITM campus.
- **PM-Vidyalaxmi:** This is the government portal for applying for education loans: https://pmvidyalaxmi.co.in/
  - You can submit one common application to up to three banks.
  - Students admitted to IITM on merit may be eligible for a loan without collateral or a guarantor under the applicable scheme.
  - The bank still checks your application and decides whether to approve the loan.
- **IITM financial support:** Scholarships, fee reductions and some interest-free loans may also be available. Check the latest scholarship/financial-aid notices rather than relying on old information.

**Applying directly through a bank**

You can approach a bank directly to ask about its education loan process.

1. Contact the bank and ask about its **education loan for IITM students**.
2. Check the loan amount, interest rate, repayment terms, required documents and costs covered.
3. Submit the bank's application and required documents.
4. The bank verifies your details and decides whether to approve the loan.
5. If approved, read the **loan sanction/offer letter** carefully before signing.
6. Ask the bank how to request the loan amount for each semester and how the payment will be made to IITM.

**Tip:** Even if you approach a bank directly, ask whether it requires you to apply through **PM-Vidyalaxmi** for your particular loan or scheme.

**Applying through PM-Vidyalaxmi**

1. Go to **PM-Vidyalaxmi:** https://pmvidyalaxmi.co.in/
2. Register and complete the **common education loan application**.
3. Upload the required documents and select the bank(s) you want to apply to.
4. Submit the application and use **Track Loan Application** to follow its status.
5. If the bank asks for additional documents or information, provide them through the process requested.

**You may need:** academic mark sheets, IITM admission proof, fee details, income proof, Aadhaar and other identity/address documents. The exact requirements can vary by scheme and bank.

**Paying IITM fees through an education loan**

For each semester:

- Check the **latest IITM fee circular** for the amount and payment instructions.
- Enter the required bank-payment details in IITM's **Integrated Fee Payment Portal (IFPP):** https://fees.iitm.ac.in/
- The bank generally sends the institute-fee amount directly to IITM.
- Keep your bank payment/transfer proof until the payment is reflected in your IITM fee record.

**After your loan is approved**

Before signing, make sure you understand:

- Interest rate
- When interest starts
- When repayment starts
- EMI amount and repayment period
- Any additional charges
- Whether you are eligible for an interest subsidy

Interest can continue to accumulate during your studies or the moratorium period, depending on your loan terms.

**Who can help?**

- **Loan-related questions:** Contact the bank you selected.
- **Bonafide certificate or academic documents:** Academic Courses Section — **helpdeskcourses@iitm.ac.in**
- **Fee-payment issues:** Check IFPP and the latest IITM fee circular for the appropriate contact.
- **PM-Vidyalaxmi issues:** Use the help/complaint option on the portal.

**Important:** Always use the latest IITM fee circular, the bank's current loan terms and the official PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.

Never share your **OTP or banking login details**.

This guide covers the main ways IITM students can go abroad during/after BTech.

Programs, partner universities and deadlines change every year, so **always check OGE for the latest information.**

Almost everything is handled through the **Office of Global Engagement (OGE)**:
https://ge.iitm.ac.in

## The 4 routes

**1. Semester Exchange**
Study one semester at an IITM partner university and transfer credits back to IITM.

**2. Research Internships & Summer/Winter Programs**
Short-term research internships, summer schools, winter schools, etc.

**3. OGE Travel Grant**
Partial reimbursement of travel costs for eligible international academic activities.

**4. Higher Studies after BTech**
Information about Master's/PhD opportunities, scholarships and fellowships abroad.

## 1. Semester Exchange

You study for around **5–6 months** at an IITM partner university and transfer eligible courses back to IITM.

### Basic criteria
- Usually **3–4 semesters completed**
- **No backlogs**
- **CGPA 7.5+ preferred**
- Higher CGPA may get priority if many students apply for the same university.

### Process
**1.** Choose **one** partner university from the OGE list.
**2.** Check its courses, teaching language and semester dates.
**3.** Discuss course mapping with your **Faculty Advisor**.
**4.** Submit the OGE nomination form before the deadline.
**5.** Your Faculty Advisor approves it.
**6.** OGE nominates you. The host university makes the final decision.

Partner list:
https://ge.iitm.ac.in/programs/student-outbound/semester-exchange/opportunities

Guidelines & FAQ:
https://ge.iitm.ac.in/programs/student-outbound/semester-exchange

## Semester Exchange — Money & Paperwork

### Money

Semester exchange is **self-funded**. IITM does not provide a regular stipend.

You generally pay for:
- Travel
- Visa
- Insurance
- Accommodation
- Food/living expenses

Some partner universities offer scholarships. The **OGE Travel Grant** may also help with eligible travel costs.

### Academic paperwork

For NOC, credit transfer and related paperwork:

**helpdeskcourses@iitm.ac.in**

**NOC for going abroad:**
- Faculty Advisor approval
- HOD approval
- Global Engagement Office approval
- Passport copy

**Credit transfer after returning:**
- Course mapping approved by your Faculty Advisor
- Host university transcript

**English test:**
If the host university asks for IELTS/TOEFL, you can usually request a **Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate** from the Academic Section, subject to the host university's requirements.

### Important rules

- Once a university confirms you, you **cannot withdraw and switch**.
- Dropping out after processing can make you ineligible for future exchanges.
- Final-semester exchange is **not recommended** and needs department approval.
- DD students also need their **project guide's approval**.
- Returning mid-semester is generally not allowed except in an emergency. Inform OGE and the host university if this happens.

## 2. Research Internships & Summer/Winter Programs

These are usually shorter opportunities, ranging from **a few weeks to around 3 months**, often during summer.

Depending on the program, it may provide:
- Tuition waiver
- Accommodation
- Stipend
- Other financial support

Some summer schools may instead charge a fee.

### Finding opportunities

OGE posts opportunities on its website and through emails, often tagged:

**[OGE]**
**[International Opportunities]**

Some programs require an **internal IITM nomination** and Faculty Advisor approval. Others allow direct applications.

**Start early:** many deadlines are several months before the program.

## 3. OGE Travel Grant

The OGE Travel Grant provides **partial reimbursement of travel expenses** for eligible international academic activities.

It may cover:
- Conferences
- Workshops
- Research visits
- Summer/winter schools
- Competitions
- Internships
- Semester exchange

### Things to remember
- Apply **after the trip**
- It is a **reimbursement**, not an advance
- The activity must be related to your **field of study**
- Students are expected to explore **other funding sources**

Details:
https://ge.iitm.ac.in/oge-travel-grant

## 4. Higher Studies after BTech

OGE and the **Global Engagement Council (GEC)** share information about Master's/PhD opportunities abroad.

This includes:
- Japan government scholarships
- France scholarships
- Germany scholarships
- University fellowships
- Other international funding opportunities

Watch for emails tagged **[Higher Studies]**.

### Higher Studies Bluebook

The GEC publishes a *Higher Studies Bluebook* based on information from IITM students who have gone abroad.

It includes:
- Country and program information
- Student experiences
- Application tips
- Universities/programs where IITM students were admitted

Search your IITM mail for **"Higher Studies Bluebook"** for the latest edition.

### Whom to contact?

**Exchange programs**
exg_prog@ge.iitm.ac.in
Or the contact listed on the OGE exchange page.

**Student guidance / info sessions / past exchange experiences**
gecouncil@smail.iitm.ac.in
Global Engagement Council

**NOC / credit transfer / bonafide**
helpdeskcourses@iitm.ac.in
Academic Courses Section

### Tips
- Keep your **CGPA up** and avoid backlogs.
- Get your **passport early**.
- Attend GEC's semester-exchange info session.
- Start looking for opportunities well before deadlines.

*Rules, programs and contacts can change. Always verify the latest information on the official IITM/OGE website.*

posts.md:
**1/4 — Basics + Cashless Treatment**

## Basics

- **Insurer:** SBI General Insurance
- **TPA:** Vidal Health
- **Policy period:** July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027
- **Coverage:** ₹1 lakh per student/year
- **OPD:** Up to ₹10,000
- **Married scholars:** ₹1.5 lakh for self + family

Your insurance e-card comes by email with the subject **“WELCOME TO VIDAL HEALTH INSURANCE TPA”**.

Search your `smail` inbox if you can't find it.

## Option 1: Cashless

The easiest option is to visit a **Vidal network hospital**.

1. Find a network hospital:
https://vidalhealthtpa.com/employeeportal/networkhospital

2. Show your **insurance e-card** at the hospital's insurance/TPA desk.

3. The hospital coordinates with the insurer for eligible expenses, so you don't have to pay the covered amount upfront.

## IITM Student Health Insurance

**2/4 — Reimbursement + Important Rules**

## Option 2: Reimbursement

If you visit a hospital that isn't in the Vidal network:

1. Pay the hospital bill yourself.
2. Keep **ALL original bills, reports and the discharge summary**.
3. Fill out the **claim form** attached to the Vidal email.
4. Submit the required original documents to the **CCW office**.
5. Reimbursement is processed after the originals are received.

**CCW:** 044-22578502

> Keep copies/photos of all documents before submitting the originals.

## Important Rules

### 24-hour admission

For regular hospitalisation claims, you generally need to be **admitted for at least 24 hours**.

**OPD is the exception** — admission is not required.

### Room Rent Limits

- **Normal room:** ₹4,000/day
- **ICU:** ₹5,000/day

If you choose a room above the applicable limit, the excess amount isn't covered. Other expenses may also be affected depending on the policy terms.

## IITM Student Health Insurance

**3/4 — OPD + Usually Covered**

## OPD Coverage — ₹10,000

**OPD = Out-Patient Department.**

It covers treatment where you **visit a doctor or undergo tests and return home without being admitted**.

Under the policy, OPD covers up to **₹10,000/year** for things such as:

- Doctor consultation fees
- MRI / CT scans
- Ultrasound
- Laboratory tests

**No 24-hour admission is required for OPD.**

**Important:** For 2026–27, OPD coverage is available only to the **first 300 students who submit a claim**.

So if you plan to use the OPD benefit, don't wait unnecessarily.

## Usually Covered

- Hospitalisation
- Surgery
- Medicines during hospitalisation
- Diagnostic tests
- Expenses **30 days before admission**
- Expenses **60 days after discharge**
- Ambulance expenses up to ₹3,000
- Pre-existing diseases, with no waiting period
- In-patient treatment for mental illness
- Eye power correction surgery

## IITM Student Health Insurance

**4/4 — Backup Fund + Exclusions + Help**

## Additional ₹30 Lakh Backup Fund

A **shared ₹30 lakh backup fund** is available for certain serious cases, including:

- Cancer
- Heart-related conditions
- Accidents
- Sports injuries
- Dengue

This can be used after the student's regular **₹1 lakh coverage is exhausted**, subject to the applicable terms and availability of the shared fund.

## Not Covered

Examples include:

- Ayurveda
- Homeopathy
- Unani treatment
- Dental OPD
- Counselling-only stays
- Administrative / registration charges

## Need Help?

**Vidal Health TPA — Toll Free:**
1800-425-7878

**WhatsApp:**
Send **“Hi”** to **+91-8792971892** from your registered mobile number for your e-card and claim status.

## Important Note

The detailed coverage list above is based on the **2023–24 policy document**. Some terms may have changed for 2026–27.

For expensive treatment or a major claim, **confirm the coverage with Vidal Health before proceeding**.

> **Quick summary:**
>  Hospitalisation → usually 24+ hours
>  OPD → no admission → ₹10,000 → first 300 students
>  Cashless → Vidal network hospital
>  Reimbursement → pay first + submit original documents

posts.md:
Every hostel room has a LAN port that provides access to the institute network and the internet.

## Step 1: Connect to the LAN

- Connect the LAN cable from the wall socket to your laptop or desktop.
- Open **Command Prompt** (Windows) or **Terminal** (Linux).

Run:

**Windows**
```bash
ipconfig
```

**Linux**
```bash
ifconfig
```

Check your **IPv4 Address**.

You should receive an address like:

- `10.17.xxx.xxx` (Academic)
- `10.21.xxx.xxx` (Academic)
- `10.22.xxx.xxx` (Hostel)
- `10.23.xxx.xxx` (Residence)

If it shows **Media disconnected**, try another LAN cable.

## Step 2: Test the Network

Run:

```bash
ping cc.iitm.ac.in
```

If you receive replies similar to:

```text
64 bytes from ...
```

your network connection is working.

If not:

- Set **DNS** to **Automatic**
- Try again

## Step 3: Disable IPv6 (Windows)

1. Press **Win + R**
2. Type:

```text
ncpa.cpl
```

3. Open **Ethernet Properties**
4. Uncheck:

```text
Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6)
```

5. Click **OK**

## Step 4: Enable Internet Access

To access websites outside IIT Madras (Google, YouTube, etc.):

1. Visit **cc.iitm.ac.in**
2. Login using your **LDAP credentials**
3. Approve your current IP address

Make sure the IP shown is your system IP:

- `10.17.xxx.xxx`
- `10.21.xxx.xxx`
- `10.22.xxx.xxx`
- `10.23.xxx.xxx`

## Check Proxy Settings

If the portal shows an IP like:

```text
10.24.x.x
```

your browser is using a proxy.

Remove/disable the proxy, refresh the page, and approve your actual system IP.

## Still Not Working?

Collect the following details:

- Hostel name
- Room number
- Mobile number
- System MAC Address
- Output of `ipconfig` / `ifconfig`
- Output of `ping cc.iitm.ac.in`

Then email:

**helpdesknetworks@iitm.ac.in**

## Find Your MAC Address

**Windows**

```bash
getmac -v
```

Look for the **Physical Address** of your Ethernet adapter.
**Tip:** You need to log in to **cc.iitm.ac.in** and approve your IP whenever required to access the internet from the hostel LAN.
## website link:- https://cc.iitm.ac.in/network/instructiontoconnectlan.html

The **Inter IIT Tech Meet** is the annual technical competition where students from all **23 IITs** come together to solve real-world engineering and technology challenges.

It serves as a platform for the brightest minds across the IIT ecosystem to innovate, collaborate, and build impactful solutions to problems that can affect millions of people.

## What Happens at the Tech Meet?

Companies and organizations release challenging **problem statements**, and participating IITs form teams to work on them over a fixed preparation period.

The teams then present their solutions during the final **offline Inter IIT Tech Meet**, where they are evaluated by industry experts and professionals.

The competition bridges the gap between **academia and industry** by exposing students to real-world engineering challenges.

## Previous Sponsors & Partners

Over the years, several leading organizations have sponsored problem statements, including:

- DRDO
- ISRO
- Adobe
- WorldQuant
- Jaguar Land Rover
- Bosch
- Silicon Labs

## History

- **First Edition:** 2012
- The **12th Inter IIT Tech Meet** was hosted by **IIT Madras**.
- Hosted nearly **2,000 students** from all **23 IITs**.
- IIT Madras has consistently secured podium finishes across multiple events.
- The **AI Contingent** from IIT Madras has achieved **podium finishes for three consecutive editions**.

## Event Categories

Events are classified based on the preparation time required.

### High Prep
- Preparation: **6–8 weeks**
- Large teams working on complex, multi-stage problems.
- Highest point value in the competition.

### Mid Prep
- Preparation: **4–6 weeks**
- Focused technical challenges requiring strong domain expertise.

### Low Prep
- Preparation: **6–10 days**
- Fast-paced events that test technical skills under tight deadlines.

### No Prep
- Preparation: **24 hours**
- Problem statements are revealed at the venue.
- Participants build solutions within a single day.

## Domains

Problem statements span a wide range of emerging technologies, including:

- Artificial Intelligence (AI)
- Blockchain
- Cybersecurity
- Sustainability
- Aeronautics
- Quantitative Finance (Quant)
- Entrepreneurship
- Product Development

...and many more cutting-edge domains.

## How to Participate

Every year, IIT Madras selects student teams through **contingent recruitment and selection processes**.

Students from diverse technical backgrounds are encouraged to participate, making the Tech Meet an excellent opportunity to:

- Solve real-world industry problems.
- Collaborate with talented peers.
- Represent IIT Madras at the national level.
- Build technical, research, and product development skills.
> **Whether you're passionate about AI, cybersecurity, product development, or entrepreneurship, the Inter IIT Tech Meet is one of the best opportunities to showcase your skills and represent IIT Madras on the national stage. **

## What are Tech Guilds?

Tech Guilds are student communities where you can learn, build, compete, and represent the institute in prestigious national and international competitions, including the **Inter IIT Tech Meet**.

- Attend regular training sessions and workshops

- Book Bank
- Back volumes in Humanities, Social Sciences, Management, Engineering, Technology, and Science

### Timings

## Floor-by-Floor Guide

## Ground Floor

- Circulation Desk (Book Issue & Return)
- Reference Section

## First Floor

A spacious and well-ventilated reading hall with:

- Bright natural lighting
- Campus views

A great place for focused individual study.

These floors feature:

- Row-by-row seating
- Bookshelves throughout

The **Third Floor** is one of the most preferred study spaces because it offers:

- Air-conditioned seating
- Good lighting
- Charging ports

- Nearby washrooms

Seats fill up quickly during exam season, so arriving early is recommended.

- Elsevier ScienceDirect
- Springer
- Wiley
- Nature

**LitSoc (Literary Society)** is the year-long **inter-hostel cultural championship** at IIT Madras.

Hostels compete against each other throughout the academic year in a variety of cultural events, earning points to compete for the **LitSoc Cup**.

Although LitSoc originally consisted only of literary competitions, it has grown over the years to include a wide range of cultural events across multiple disciplines.

## Events & Competitions

Around **40 events** are conducted every year as part of LitSoc.

The competition begins with **Queen of Sheba**, a flagship event that combines a **treasure hunt** with a celebration of hostel spirit.

- **Even Semester:** More group events

Some of the most popular LitSoc events include:

- Queen of Sheba

- Short Film Making & Screening
- Band Performances
- And many more.

Winners receive **certificates and medals**, and events are judged by experts from outside the institute.

Outstanding performances have even led to opportunities for students to perform outside the institute.

## Hostel Bonding Through LitSoc

LitSoc is more than just a competition—it is an important part of the hostel experience.

Students who may not have known each other often come together to represent their hostel, building friendships while competing for valuable points.

Information about events is shared through:

- Club Instagram pages
- Sangam Instagram pages
- Official student emails
- Event posters and rulebooks

Freshers who actively participate throughout LitSoc are also recognized with **special awards** for contributing points to their hostel.

## Why LitSoc?

LitSoc encourages students to explore new forms of art, develop their talents, and step outside their comfort zones.

It offers opportunities to:

- Try new cultural activities
- Earn participation and competition points
- Cheer for your hostel during events
- Celebrate your hostel's achievements

For many students, watching their hostel lift the **LitSoc Championship Trophy** is one of the most memorable moments of campus life.

The friendships, experiences, and hostel spirit built during LitSoc become lasting memories long after graduation.

IIT Madras has **three major mess complexes**:

- Himalaya
- Vindhya
- Nilgiri

Together, they house **10–11 messes and food courts**, offering students a wide variety of meal options throughout the academic year.

The messes are designed to provide nutritious, hygienic, and diverse meals that cater to the needs of students from across the country.

## What Do the Messes Provide?

The messes are modern and student-friendly, featuring **face-scan biometric access** for seamless entry.

Across campus food courts, students can conveniently make payments using their **Institute ID cards**.

To cater to the diverse student community, IIT Madras has:

- North Indian Messes
- South Indian Messes
- Unified Messes serving both cuisines
- A Jain Mess for students who prefer Jain food

Students can choose familiar food from home or explore different cuisines.

The messes aim to meet the dietary requirements of all students without compromising on quality or nutrition.

## Mess Registration

Mess registration is managed through the **iKollege Portal**.

The system helps:

- Reduce food wastage by informing caterers about the expected number of diners.
- Ensure students do not pay for meals they do not consume.

## How to Register

Students can register for their preferred mess through the **iKollege Portal** during the dates announced by the **Office of Hostel Management**.

Students submit their mess preferences in order of choice.

Every effort is made to allot the **first preference**. However, if a mess reaches its capacity, students may be allotted another preference.

Mess allocation follows a **first-come, first-served** basis.

Students are also allowed to **change their mess** periodically (typically every one or two months).

Students staying on campus during vacations can also register for messes through the portal, provided they have the necessary accommodation and permission from the concerned authorities.

## What Makes IIT Madras' Mess System Unique?

Unlike many institutes where each hostel has its own mess, IIT Madras has **large common dining halls**, some with seating capacities of up to **1500 students**.

This allows students to interact with people from different hostels, departments, and academic years during meals.

The weekly menu offers sufficient variety to avoid monotony, and the food is also appreciated by many international students.

Students can also claim **mess rebates** for valid reasons such as:

- Ramadan fasting
- Health issues requiring recovery away from the Institute

The mess system is continuously improved in terms of food quality, management, and seating capacity to provide better services to students.

posts.md:
A **Minor** is an academic credential awarded by IIT Madras that certifies your proficiency in a **secondary field of study** in addition to your major.

It appears on your **official transcript**, demonstrating that you have completed a structured set of courses in another discipline alongside your primary degree.

A minor is an excellent way to explore areas beyond your core branch and build interdisciplinary knowledge.

## Minor System at IIT Madras

Earlier, students had to formally register for a minor in advance. However, with the introduction of a wider range of electives, the system became much more flexible.

Under the current system:

- There is **no need to register for a minor beforehand.**
- You can gradually complete the required courses while planning your electives.
- Once all the requirements are met, you can claim the minor.

Each minor consists of:

- A set of mandatory (core) courses.
- A list of elective courses.

Typically, students need to complete **4 courses (approximately 36–40 credits)** to earn a minor, although the exact requirements vary depending on the discipline.

Some minors may require:
- 1 core course + 3 electives.
- 2 core courses + 2 electives.
- Other combinations as specified by the department.

## Available Minor Areas

Students can pursue minors in a wide variety of disciplines, including:

- Artificial Intelligence
- Machine Learning
- Applied Economics
- Mathematics
- International Relations
- Sociology

...and many other fields offered by different departments.

## How to Claim a Minor

Once you have:

- Completed all the required courses, or
- Are currently enrolled in the remaining required courses,

you can apply for the minor by **emailing the Dean (Academic Courses)** during the designated claiming period.

The minor will then be added to your academic transcript after verification.

## Planning Your Minor

Most B.Tech. programmes require careful academic planning to fit a minor into the available free credits.

Keep in mind:

- Most engineering curricula require around **72–90 unallocated credits** to comfortably accommodate a minor.
- Humanities elective requirements also need to be considered while planning.
- It is recommended to complete the minor requirements by the **7th semester** so that it can be officially recorded before graduation.

Since course prerequisites and scheduling differ across departments, it is advisable to start planning your minor by the **3rd or 4th semester**.

## Can NPTEL Courses Be Used?

Yes.

Certain **NPTEL courses** can be counted towards a minor, subject to institute regulations and credit transfer limits.

Since there is a cap on the number of transferable NPTEL credits, students should plan their usage carefully.

With proper planning, it is even theoretically possible to complete **more than one minor**.

## Does Your Branch Matter?

No.

Your **major branch does not restrict your choice of minor**.

You are free to pursue:

- A minor closely related to your branch.
- A completely different discipline.

The only requirement is that you successfully complete all the courses specified for that minor.

There is also **no fixed order** in which minor courses must be taken, except where course prerequisites apply.

## Why Pursue a Minor?

## Better Career Opportunities

A minor demonstrates additional expertise in a particular field, making your profile more attractive to recruiters.

It shows employers that you have invested time in developing knowledge beyond your primary discipline.

## Helpful for Higher Studies

A minor is particularly valuable if you plan to pursue **Master's or Ph.D. programmes** in a field different from your undergraduate branch (commonly called **cross-apping**).

Having a minor in the target field strengthens your academic profile and supports your application.

## Explore Your Interests

A minor allows you to study subjects that genuinely interest you, even if they are unrelated to your major.

Whether you're interested in AI, Economics, Finance, Public Policy, Mathematics, or the Social Sciences, a minor provides a structured way to gain deeper knowledge.

## Final Thoughts

A minor is **not mandatory**, but it can significantly enhance your academic profile, broaden your skill set, and open up new career and higher education opportunities.

If you're considering pursuing one, start exploring your interests and planning your electives early so that you have enough credits to complete the requirements before graduation.

posts.md:
Apart from regular offline institute courses, **B.Tech and Dual Degree students can also take eligible online courses through NPTEL and Online BS (OB) programmes**.

These courses can help you complete credits required for your degree, subject to the applicable rules.

## NPTEL Courses

**NPTEL (National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning)** offers online courses that B.Tech and Dual Degree students can use to earn credits towards their degree.

### Course Details

* **Mode of learning:** Online
* **Mode of exam:** Offline
* **Exam structure:** One final exam
* **Credits:** Count towards your degree
* **CGPA:** NPTEL grades **do not affect your CGPA**

**NPTEL / SWAYAM:** https://swayam.gov.in/

## Which Category Do NPTEL Credits Count Towards?

NPTEL courses can generally be transferred under the **Unallotted category**.

However, **some NPTEL courses can fulfil credits under the HS (Humanities & Sciences) category**.

>  Only NPTEL/SWAYAM courses that are **classified under the HS category on the NPTEL/SWAYAM portal** can be transferred to the **HS category** in your curriculum.

So, before registering, **check the category listed for the course on the NPTEL/SWAYAM portal**.

**Course category on NPTEL/SWAYAM → determines the curriculum category to which the credits can be transferred.**

## NPTEL Fees

* **Course learning:** Generally free
* **Certification exam:** Paid
* You need to pay an **exam registration fee** to appear for the NPTEL certification exam.
* The exam fee may vary, so check the official SWAYAM/NPTEL portal while registering.

## NPTEL Credit Transfer

After successfully passing the NPTEL certification exam:

### 1. Receive your certificate

You will receive an **NPTEL certificate** after successfully completing the certification requirements.

### 2. Raise a ticket in Workflow

After receiving the certificate, **raise a ticket in Workflow** to request the transfer of your NPTEL credits to your curriculum.

### 3. Credits are transferred

Once the process is completed, the credits will be counted towards the **applicable curriculum category**.

For example:

* **Regular NPTEL course → Unallotted**
* **NPTEL course classified as HS → HS category**

>  **Important:** Passing the NPTEL exam does not automatically transfer the credits to your curriculum. You need to raise the required ticket through Workflow after receiving your certificate.

### In short

**NPTEL Course → Final Exam → Pass → Certificate → Raise Workflow Ticket → Credits Transferred**

## Online BS (OB) Courses

B.Tech and Dual Degree students can also take eligible courses offered through the **Online BS programmes**.

These courses can count towards your **Unallotted credits**.

### Course Details

* **Mode of learning:** Online
* **Mode of exam:** Offline
* **Credits:** Count towards your degree
* **CGPA:** Grades earned in OB courses **are included in your CGPA**
* **Seat limitation:** **No seat limitations**

## Course & Exam Structure

The evaluation pattern **depends on the specific course**.

A course may include:

* Assignments
* Quizzes
* End-semester examination

However, the structure can vary between courses.

>  **Always check the specific course structure and assessment pattern before registering.**

## How to Register

There are **two ways** to take an Online BS course:

### 1. Summer Course

Register through the **SSP Portal**.

### 2. Regular Semester Course

Register through the **Course Registration Workflow**.

>  The Workflow works only in **Firefox** Browser.

Eligible BS courses will appear in the Workflow during course registration.

## Online BS Course Fees

For **B.Tech and Dual Degree students taking eligible Online BS courses through this provision, no additional fees are required**.

## Credit & Semester Limits

The following limits apply to **NPTEL + Online BS courses combined**:

* Maximum **36 credits** from NPTEL + Online BS courses combined
* Maximum **21 credits** out of those 36 can be from **NPTEL**
* Only **one course through this mode is permitted per semester**
* The credits must also remain within the overall **66-credit semester limit**

### Example

If you take a **12-credit OB course**:

**12 credits → Unallotted category**
**Grade → Included in CGPA**

If you take a **9-credit NPTEL course**:

**9 credits → Applicable category**
**Grade → Not included in CGPA**

If the NPTEL course is classified as **HS on SWAYAM**, the credits can be transferred to your **HS category**.

## Important Things to Remember

* **NPTEL + OB courses together are limited to 36 credits.**
* Maximum **21 credits** can be from NPTEL.
* Only **one NPTEL/OB course per semester** can be taken through this provision.
* The overall semester limit of **66 credits** still applies.
* **NPTEL grades do not affect CGPA.**
* **OB grades are included in CGPA.**
* Most NPTEL courses can be transferred under **Unallotted**.
* NPTEL courses classified as **HS on SWAYAM/NPTEL** can be transferred to the **HS category**.
* Always check the **NPTEL/SWAYAM course category before registering**.
* After receiving your NPTEL certificate, you must **raise a Workflow ticket for credit transfer**.
* Eligible OB courses will appear in the **Course Registration Workflow**.
* OB and NPTEL courses have **no seat limitations**.
* The list of available OB courses may change when new Online BS programmes are introduced.
* OB courses follow the programme's rules and assessment requirements strictly, so **check the course-specific details before registering**.

## In Simple Terms

### NPTEL

**Online Course**
↓
**Offline Final Exam**
↓
**Pass**
↓
**Receive Certificate**
↓
**Raise Workflow Ticket**
↓
**Credits Transferred**

**CGPA impact:**  No

**Category:** Usually **Unallotted**, but eligible courses classified as **HS on SWAYAM/NPTEL** can be transferred to **HS**.

### Online BS (OB)

**Online Course**
↓
**Course-specific Assessments**
↓
**Offline Exam**
↓
**Credits + Grade**
↓
**Counts towards your curriculum**

**CGPA impact:**  Yes

**Category:** **Unallotted**

>  **In short:**
> **NPTEL → Earn credits without affecting CGPA**
> **NPTEL (HS course) → Can fulfil HS credits**
> **Online BS → Earn credits and the grade contributes to CGPA**

## NPTEL vs Online BS (OB)

## NPTEL

**Learning:** Online
**Exam:** Offline
**Evaluation:** One final exam
**Credits:** Count towards your degree
**Category:** Usually Unallotted
**HS:** Some courses can fulfil HS credits if they are classified as **HS on NPTEL/SWAYAM**
**CGPA:**  Does not affect CGPA
**Exam fee:** Paid
**Credit transfer:** Receive certificate → Raise Workflow ticket
**Credit limit:** Maximum 21 NPTEL credits

## Online BS (OB)

**Learning:** Online
**Exam:** Offline
**Evaluation:** Depends on the course
**Credits:** Count towards your degree
**Category:** Unallotted
**CGPA:**  Grades affect CGPA
**Fee:** No additional fee for eligible on-campus students
**Seats:** No seat limitation
**Registration:** SSP for summer / Workflow for regular semester

## Common Rules

These rules apply to **NPTEL + Online BS courses combined**:

* Maximum **36 credits** combined
* Maximum **21 credits** can be from NPTEL
* Only **one course per semester** through this provision
* Credits count towards the applicable curriculum category
* Overall **66-credit semester limit** still applies

## Which One Should You Choose?

### Choose NPTEL if:

You want to **earn credits without affecting your CGPA**.

**Online → Offline final exam → Pass → Certificate → Workflow ticket → Credits**

### Choose Online BS if:

You want to **earn credits and have the course grade contribute to your CGPA**.

**Online → Course-specific assessments → Offline exam → Credits + Grade**

### Want HS Credits?

For NPTEL, **check the course category on SWAYAM/NPTEL before registering**.

Only courses classified as **HS** can be transferred to the **HS category** in your curriculum.

## National Sports Organisation (NSO)

**NSO (National Sports Organisation)** is one of the institute programmes that every undergraduate student at IIT Madras must complete during their first year.

Along with **NSS (National Service Scheme)**, **NCC (National Cadet Corps)**, and **NCA (National Cultural Activities)**, NSO is designed to encourage the holistic development of students beyond academics.

Successful completion of one of these programmes is **mandatory** for the completion of your degree.

## What is NSO?

NSO provides students with **structured training and coaching** in a sport or physical activity of their choice as part of the institute curriculum.

Students are expected to:

- Attend regular training sessions across **two semesters**.
- Participate actively in their chosen sport.
- Successfully complete the programme to fulfill the institute requirement.

Training is conducted by **experienced coaches** using IIT Madras' extensive sports facilities.

## Sports Offered

Students can choose from a variety of sports and activities, including:

- Athletics
- Badminton
- Basketball
- Chess
- Cricket
- Football
- Frisbee
- Hockey
- Lawn Tennis
- Skating
- Squash
- Swimming
- Table Tennis
- Volleyball
- Weightlifting
- Yoga
- Fitness & Recreational Activities

> *The list of available sports may vary slightly each year.*

## Why is NSO Important?

NSO is more than just a compulsory course—it is an opportunity to:

- Improve your physical fitness.
- Develop teamwork and leadership skills.
- Build discipline and consistency.
- Learn a new sport or improve existing skills.
- Maintain a healthy and active lifestyle.

## Beyond NSO

For many students, NSO serves as their introduction to the vibrant sports culture at IIT Madras.

It often inspires students to:

- Represent their hostel in **Schroeter (Inter-Hostel Sports)**.
- Participate in institute-level tournaments.
- Try out for the **Inter IIT Sports Meet** contingent.
- Continue playing sports throughout their time at IIT Madras.

> **Whether you're an experienced athlete or trying a sport for the first time, NSO is a great way to stay active, make friends, and become a part of IIT Madras' thriving sports culture.**

## National Service Scheme (NSS)

The **National Service Scheme (NSS)** is a voluntary organization that encourages students and youth to participate in community service.

At IIT Madras, NSS has an active volunteer community that runs several projects, enabling students to make a positive impact on the surrounding community.

## First-Year Participation

First-year students who enrol in NSS are allotted a **project team**, where they contribute towards various community service initiatives.

Students can earn credits through:

- Project milestones
- Winter internships
- Lectures
- Movie screenings
- Awareness campaigns organized by the NSS managerial team

## Beyond the First Year

Students can continue volunteering even after completing their compulsory first-year service.

They can also take up **managerial positions** within the NSS team and contribute to organizing projects and events.

## Contact

For any queries, contact:

**Email:** `adnss@smail.iitm.ac.in`

## National Cultural Academy (NCA)

The **National Cultural Academy (NCA)** is a first-year curriculum programme at IIT Madras.

Rather than having its own exclusive clubs, NCA operates through **six Sangam cultural clubs**.

Weekly NCA classes and workshops are conducted by:

- Senior students from the respective Sangam clubs.
- Professional trainers hired by the institute.

## Music Club

### Role in NCA

The **Music Club** manages training in:

- Guitar
- Keyboard
- Western Vocals

### Activities

- Conducts freshers' NCA auditions.
- Coordinates weekly lessons.
- Organizes beginner jam circles.

## Classical Arts Club

### Role in NCA

The **Classical Arts Club** manages training in:

- Carnatic Vocals
- Bharatanatyam

### Activities

Provides foundational classical training for students completing their first-year NCA requirements.

## Thespian (Drama Club)

### Role in NCA

The **Thespian (Drama Club)** oversees the **Dramatics / Theatre** vertical.

### Activities

- Acting workshops
- Scriptwriting sessions
- Dialogue delivery training
- Annual NCA Dramatics Showcase

The club also collaborates with external theatre groups.

## Choreo Club

### Role in NCA

The **Choreo Club** manages the:

- Western Dance
- Contemporary Dance

### Activities

Organizes weekly choreography workshops for both beginners and intermediate dancers.

## Fine Arts Club

### Role in NCA

The **Fine Arts Club** coordinates the **Fine Arts** vertical.

### Activities

Students receive training in:

- Sketching
- Canvas Painting
- Collaborative Art Installations

## Media / Design & VFX Club

### Role in NCA

The **Media / Design & VFX Club** oversees the:

- Film-Making
- Design

training tracks.

### Activities

Students learn:

- Camera Mechanics
- Video Editing
- Graphic Design Principles

## National Cadet Corps (NCC)

The **National Cadet Corps (NCC)** is the civilian youth wing of the **Indian Armed Forces**, aiming to instill discipline, leadership, and patriotism among students.

At IIT Madras, **NCC** is a **credit-earning, pass/fail first-year graduation requirement**. First-year students can choose **NCC** as an alternative to **NSS**, **NSO**, or **NCA**.

## Programme Overview

- Functions as a mandatory first-year activity with a **Pass/Fail** evaluation.
- Students must meet the required attendance criteria to earn a **Pass** grade.
- The programme focuses on discipline, parade drills, camps, and service training.

## Activities & Training

NCC cadets participate in:

- Parade drills for **Independence Day** and **Republic Day** celebrations.
- NCC training based on the applicable **Army, Navy, or Air Force** syllabus.
- Training camps.
- Survival skills training.

## Squadron

The IIT Madras NCC unit primarily operates as an **Air Force Technical Squadron**, with routine drill sessions conducted in addition to preparations for national celebrations.

**Email:** `adncc@smail.iitm.ac.in`

## About POSH Training: A Student Guide

## What is POSH?

POSH stands for *Prevention of Sexual Harassment*. It is the framework for preventing and addressing sexual harassment.

POSH training is a **compulsory, zero-credit course**.

- It does not add to your credit total.
- Completion appears on your grade card.

## Who needs to complete it?

The training is compulsory for **all students**.

- **B.Tech and PhD students must repeat it after two years.**
- For PG students and research scholars, non-completion can also affect scholarships.

If you are unsure whether you need to repeat it, check your programme requirement or contact the **CCASH Office**.

## How to Register

1. Watch your institute email for a POSH/CCASH training announcement.
2. Register through the POSH portal: https://posh.iitm.ac.in/
3. Check your confirmation email for the **date, time and venue**.
4. Attend the **same session you registered for**.
5. Only students registered through the portal can attend the in-person session.

Try to attend your assigned session to avoid issues with your completion certificate.

## How to Complete the Training

Attending the in-person training is **not the only requirement**.

After the training:

1. You will receive a link for a **post-training e-module assessment** on your registered email.
2. Complete the assessment and obtain the required passing score.
3. A **Pass** grade will then be recorded on your grade card.
4. Download your **training-completion certificate** from the POSH portal.

If you do not pass the assessment, follow the training office's instructions to **register again and re-attend the training**.

## What is CCASH?

CCASH stands for **Complaints Committee Against Sexual Harassment**.

It handles **POSH-related matters and complaints**.

CCASH follows a **confidential and impartial process** and includes faculty members, student representatives and an external expert.

If you experience sexual harassment, you can approach **CCASH** and submit a written complaint.

You can also seek confidential support from **YourDOST or an Institute Counsellor**.

## If You Experience Harassment

- Preserve relevant records such as messages, emails, photos, videos or social-media posts.
- You can submit a **written complaint to CCASH**.
- You can approach a **CCASH committee member**.
- You do not need to feel embarrassed or ashamed about seeking help or making a complaint.

**Remember:** You have the right to seek help and report harassment.

## If Someone Tells You They Were Harassed

If a friend or someone you know tells you about harassment:

- Listen without blaming or judging them.
- Let them speak without interruption.
- Ask what support they want instead of telling them what to do.
- Offer to accompany them if they decide to report.
- Respect their decision and continue to support them.

## CCASH & POSH Contacts

**In danger right now?** Call campus Security: +91 44 2257 9999

**CCASH Office:** Above Cafe Coffee Day (CCD), next to the Department of Management Studies.

**CCASH:** `ccash@iitm.ac.in`

**POSH:** `poshtraining@smail.iitm.ac.in`

For questions about registration, training sessions, missed sessions, assessment or certificates, contact the **POSH Training Office**.

IIT Madras follows a zero-tolerance policy towards ragging. Every student has the right to feel safe on campus. If you experience or witness ragging, report it immediately—your identity and safety are taken seriously.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

What Counts as Ragging?

Ragging includes any behavior that humiliates, threatens, or harms another student, including:

Mental, physical, or sexual abuse
Verbal abuse or insulting language
Indecent or humiliating behavior
Criminal intimidation or wrongful restraint
Financial exploitation or extortion
Any act that undermines a student's dignity

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Consequences of Ragging

Students found involved in ragging may face one or more of the following actions:

Cancellation of admission
Suspension from attending classes
Withdrawal of scholarships or fellowships
Debarment from representing IIT Madras in competitions, tournaments, or festivals
Collective disciplinary action if the individuals responsible cannot be identified

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Need Help?

If you experience or witness ragging, contact any of the following immediately:

24×7 Ragging Helpline: 044-2257-9999
Alternate Number: 044-2257-8280
Email: secsec@iitm.ac.in

You can also reach out to:

Your Hostel Warden
Chairman/Vice Chairman, Council of Wardens (CCW)
DoST (Dean of Students) Office

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Senior's Advice
Save the ragging helpline number on your phone before arriving on campus.
If something feels uncomfortable, don't assume it's "normal" or "part of college life." Report it early.
If a friend is being ragged, encourage them to seek help—you can report incidents even as a witness.

This guide provides an overview of the student bodies that function under the Research Affairs Secretary.

Scholar Support & Wellbeing

posts.md:
The **IIT Madras Research Park** is a hub for innovation, research, and entrepreneurship, serving both the institute and the larger industry.

Spread over **11.42 acres**, the Research Park consists of **5 towers** and provides over **1.2 million square feet of workspace** for:

- 16 Departments
- 600+ Faculty Members
- 3,500 Research Scholars

With well-equipped laboratories and testing facilities, it provides an ideal environment for turning innovative ideas into reality.

## Innovation & Startups

The IIT Madras Research Park has incubated **close to 200 startups** through the nodal **IITM Incubator**.

It represents the success, scale, and innovation that IIT Madras can bring to promising ideas.

Many homegrown startups originating from IIT Madras have benefited from the Research Park's facilities, ecosystem, and mentorship.

## Opportunities for Students

Students interested in research, innovation, or entrepreneurship can work with the **IIT Madras Research Park** as:

- Project Associates
- Interns

These opportunities provide hands-on experience, exposure to cutting-edge innovation, and help students develop entrepreneurial and research skills.
## Website Link:- https://respark.iitm.ac.in/
## You Tube video:- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xO9rsk7nnY

## Interning at IIT Madras Research Park

Interning at the **IIT Madras Research Park (IITM RP)** is a great way to gain hands-on experience in a cutting-edge research and innovation ecosystem.

For IIT Madras students, internship opportunities at startups within the Research Park are frequently shared through the **student email**. Students can directly apply for roles that match their interests and skills.

## Finding Internship Opportunities

Students can also explore internship opportunities by visiting the **official IITM Research Park website**.

The website provides information about:

- Ongoing work at the Research Park
- Internship opportunities (when available)
- Companies operating within IITM RP

Many companies at the Research Park are open to interacting with IIT Madras students about their research and potential internship opportunities.

Students are encouraged to reach out to companies directly or visit the Research Park to discuss possible internship roles.

## Networking Matters

Building a strong network can significantly improve your chances of securing an internship at IITM Research Park.

Useful connections include:

- Professors
- Alumni
- Seniors

Many of them have ties with companies at IITM Research Park and can help connect students with internship opportunities.

Networking early during your time at IIT Madras can go a long way in opening doors to research and industry experiences.
